title: Serve a shareable bilingual portfolio from Astro with and without the 3D island

scope.subject: Use existing Astro content and static pages to give the authored Personal Universe work an index/detail, plain navigation from the HUD, and a non-WebGL / no-JavaScript homepage fallback, with no changes to galaxy, camera or renderer ownership.

research_summary: Main already owns an Astro portfolio Content Collection, a bilingual React HUD and canonical product navigation. PR #180 adds canonical JSON content identity/bilingual values but no public work routes. A full template or managed portfolio would introduce a second site/theme/content owner; ordinary Astro static paths and semantic HTML supply all needed routing and fallback while keeping the immersive island unchanged.

sources.finding: A mature Astro/Markdown theme supplies a whole installable blog and portfolio-like site, with its own layout, configuration and collections. Available to study rather than copy the entire site.

Astro getCollection reads the existing entry schema and can filter non-public rows at build time. Astro render presents existing Markdown entries without creating a content service or executing client navigation.
Static getStaticPaths plus a rest route can prerender the collection index and each detail; both language URLs are actual HTML pages, not client history entries.

A CSS relational selector can limit the static fallback to the absence of the mounted island root without introducing another WebGL probe or subscribing to the engine. A noscript rule explicitly disables the stale island on no-JavaScript sessions.
Build links from import.meta.env.BASE_URL to support GitHub Pages under a repository subpath as well as root-local builds.
Use the existing Playwright lifecycle to create JavaScript-disabled/mobile sessions and Chromium opt-out of WebGL; validate actual plain links as well as the normal canvas route.

search_ladder.conclusion: A downloadable Astro site could stand up a text portfolio, but duplicates the already working product shell and Content Collection to solve two small read routes.
Static Astro routing, existing content, native URLs and the established acceptance runner cover build-time identity, language, mobile/Pages portability and end-to-end fallback.
Reuse the one authored collection and canonical ID; no additional content loader, CMS, i18n package or 3D state machine.
Use plain browser hyperlinks, a normal noscript branch, and the repository's existing authored/preview assets. No fallback canvas or generated marketing assets.

candidates.name: Astro Cactus starter
candidates.reason: A separate theme and content topology would displace the existing 3D homepage or duplicate the Astro build for a tiny native entry/detail flow.

candidates.name: Astro static collection routes and native HTML
candidates.source: Existing project Astro installation and Content Collection
candidates.reason: Produces static links and details from the current authored data, respects non-public rows and reuses the same identity across Markdown→canonical JSON.

candidates.name: Existing Astro base-aware URLs
candidates.reason: Gives the HUD and static pages working root/subpath deeplinks and canonical language URLs without another URL configuration or router.

candidates.name: Existing Playwright browser tests
candidates.reason: Validates actual visitors with disabled JS or disabled WebGL, bilingual routes, HTML on the project subpath and ordinary 3D rendering using established fixtures.

decision.rationale: Keep one published collection and one live 3D authority; only add native static read-side presentation and an ordinary link from the already bilingual HUD. Text fallback is outside the island and remains readable if the rendering tree is removed.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: A general portfolio theme is helpful for a greenfield site, not for a self-contained companion to an existing immersive page with an approved content authority.

decision.fallback: If the CSS relational selector is unavailable, the static entry remains server-generated and reachable directly, and the explicit no-JavaScript fallback still works; do not introduce a second WebGL context just to detect availability.
